result.process_summary: Both the tour guide and the AI serve as authoritative narrators for an audience. In each case the narrator may generate information that appears credible (tall tales or plausible‑sounding output) but is actually false, causing the audience to be misled.
potential_breaks: A human tour guide can intentionally lie, whereas AI hallucinations are typically unintended errors.
The guide operates in a physical museum context with limited scope, while AI can produce hallucinations across any domain.
A guide can be corrected in real time by the audience or other staff; AI may lack immediate feedback mechanisms.
